claims.text: HEAs contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
The initial nanoparticles are single-phase, randomly mixed solid solutions with minimal short-range ordering.
Structural and chemical stability across 473–1923 K is governed by a balance between configurational entropy and lattice distortion from atomic-size mismatch.
An atomic-size dispersion of approximately 15% is a critical upper threshold for stability.
Moderate atomic-size mismatch creates lattice strain that raises atomic-diffusion barriers.
Higher diffusion barriers suppress phase segregation and chemical ordering under high-temperature excitation.
High configurational entropy lowers the free energy of simple solid-solution phases and makes ordered intermetallic phases less competitive, especially at high temperature.
Using elements with similar atomic radii maximizes the stabilizing effect of configurational entropy.
Excessive atomic-size mismatch reduces kinetic barriers to diffusion.
Excessive atomic-size mismatch promotes segregation or formation of intermetallic phases at elevated temperatures.
Nanoparticles with moderate atomic-size differences will retain a single-phase solid solution with minimal segregation after prolonged exposure throughout 473–1923 K.
Nanoparticles with larger atomic-size mismatches will show phase transformation, segregation, or increased short-range ordering under the same thermal exposure.
Stability is maintained when atomic-size dispersion remains below about 15% and processing preserves random mixing.
Slow cooling permits diffusion and destabilizes the solid-solution phase.
Nanoparticles made from elements with similar atomic radii have been demonstrated to remain stable single-phase solid solutions at moderate temperatures.

contradictions.description: The comparison is described as using different constituent elements to alter atomic radii while also claiming that the two batches have identical nominal compositions. Changing elemental identities changes the nominal alloy composition and introduces chemical confounders beyond size mismatch.

Moderate mismatch is said to raise diffusion barriers through lattice strain, whereas excessive mismatch is said to reduce those barriers. A nonmonotonic relationship could reconcile these statements, but no transition mechanism or evidence for the reversal is supplied.
